data.narrative:
Naïfo Technologies, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Aymeric Barthes and Gaëtan Sévérac, has raised €54.7M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private peers (including Hadrian, Agile Robots, and Nimble Robotics) and 1 public company in the robotics sector.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-Progression, using total capital raised (€54.7M) as a proxy baseline and applying a typical 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of €93M. Peer-Median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables yields a median valuation of €1.0B, with a range of €1.0B to €1.6B. These peers (Hadrian at €1.6B, Agile Robots and Nimble Robotics each at €1.0B) represent the most directly comparable reference points.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of €79M (low) to €1.1B (high), with a median of €546M. The wide spread reflects material tension between capital-raised multiples and peer-based benchmarking. The Stage-Progression method suggests more conservative valuation relative to peers, possibly indicating either that Naïfo is earlier in market traction relative to its cohort or that sector multiples have expanded beyond typical step-up assumptions. Key uncertainties include relative revenue scale and growth trajectory versus named peers, and whether public comparable metrics (277810.KQ) would tighten this range.
